entrances.note: In at the door, from the map.

repeat: The glass is new and the putty's still pale. Built well, and built for children who'd want to look out.
A teacher at that desk would see the whole town at once, and know exactly who was late.
then: Through it, the town, which is busy looking for gold and has never once glanced this way.

LISTEN_TO.say: The hammering from town, far off. Everybody is building something, and not this.
repeat: Somebody hammering, very far off. Consolation builds at all hours, except in here.
Wind across the glass. It's the only lesson the room has ever had.

LOOK_AT.say: A brass handbell on the teacher's desk, for calling in a class that hasn't come.
repeat: Polished. Somebody comes in to polish a bell that has never been rung for a class.
The handle is turned wood, and fits a hand exactly. A teacher's hand. It's waiting for one.

LISTEN_TO.say: …It's in tune. Of all the things in this town.
repeat: Still in tune. I've come back to check twice.
Nothing. I'm not going to ring it. Not for nobody.

overrides.USE: No. The first time that bell rings, it should mean something.

LOOK_AT.say: A school stove, blacked and cold, with the kindling laid ready in it.
repeat: The coal scuttle's full, and the coal's never been touched. It's the best-stocked stove in town.
A kettle on top, clean, for a teacher's tea. There's a cup beside it, for one.
then: Ready for winter, and for children.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. A cold stove sounds exactly like an empty room.
repeat: Nothing. It's waiting for winter, and for someone to be cold in front of it.
A tick of iron, cooling further. It has never once been warm.
There's chalk on the ledge, a whole new box, unopened.
The board's been oiled, so the chalk would take. It's ready for the alphabet, and the alphabet hasn't come.
then: Somebody washed a blackboard that has never been written on.

repeat: Nothing. A blackboard is quiet until somebody makes it squeak.
Nothing. I'm not going to make it squeak. It deserves better for a first word.

overrides.USE: I'd write something, but the first thing on that board ought to be the alphabet, not me.

LOOK_AT.say: Fourteen desks, made by hand, well made. Nobody has ever sat in them.
repeat: Each desk has an inkwell, filled. The ink has dried in every one, waiting.
The lids are carved: not by children, by the carpenter, with the date. Every desk is dated the same day.
Nothing. Fourteen desks, and not a whisper among them.
A lid, settling, very quietly, as if it had nearly been opened.

overrides.PUSH: They're in perfect rows. I'm not going to be the one who spoils that.

exits.name: THE DOOR

LOOK_AT.say: The schoolhouse door, on new hinges that have never once been opened by a child.
repeat: A hook on the inside for each coat. Fourteen hooks. They counted.
There's a little step outside it, low, for short legs.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing, which in a schoolhouse is the saddest sound there is.
repeat: The hinges, silent. They've been oiled, for nobody.
Nothing. It's been holding the door for a class for years.
